findings.title: File-level node selection exceeds the architecture’s defined types
findings.description: The design changes the selector to include every node except `function` and `class`, so a future or unknown node type would be treated as file-level data automatically. The architecture defines the file-level types explicitly (`file`, `config`, `service`, `endpoint`, `schema`, `table`, `pipeline`, `document`, and `resource`) and says function- and class-level nodes are not read. Use that defined set, or make an unknown type an explicit contract-drift case rather than silently widening what the skill reads.

findings.title: Dependency mapping conflicts with the graph read discipline
findings.description: The dependency-observations section says function- and class-level edge endpoints will be resolved to their owning file’s layer, so cross-layer `calls` edges are counted. The architecture’s read discipline excludes function- and class-level nodes, and this design does not explain how it can determine their owning files without reading them. Define a compliant mapping strategy, or omit those endpoints from this slice’s observations.
